market.what: curative mousy-taint treatments (yeast-hull adsorbents, e.g. SpringFix Mousy), world
market.method: est.: natural/no-SO2 wine ~1% of 226 Mhl = 2.3 Mhl x ~10% mousy = 0.23 Mhl x 40 g/hL x ~$45/kg = ~$0.4M; +cider/sour beer ~$0.1M

value.logic: est.: 0.23 Mhl mousy wine/yr x ~$1,000/hL ex-cellar (natural wine) x ~50% value lost (dump, downgrade, returns) = ~$115M; today's best fix removes only 30-46%
value.revenue_logic: treat 40% of 0.23 Mhl = 92k hL x $15/hL = $1.4M; + cider/beer ~$0.1M
value.margin_logic: tiny volume, high price per hL; binder cost ~$3-5/hL at 5-10 g/hL

trend.drivers: low/no-SO2, organic and natural wine growth (organic wine volume +7% in 2024) while total wine shrinks

indirect_startups: amaea (NZ, 2011; MIP filtration for taints, could extend)
competition.notes: Only product on market is Fermentis yeast hulls, 30-46% removal at 40 g/hL. No startup found. Research small (AWRI, ISVV Bordeaux, Campden BRI).

lab.synth: catalog core (3-phenylpyridinium class) + 2 custom 1-2 step variants, then graft on insoluble support for wine use
lab.test: spiked + real mousy wine (ATHP/ETHP/APY 20-100 ug/L); HPLC-MS (AWRI method) or SBSE-GC-MS at AWRI/ISVV; aroma GC-MS; sensory triangle test ISO 4120

sale.gates: US TTB treating-material approval + FDA food-contact for resin ~1 yr; EU needs OIV/EU 2019/934 listing (3-5 yr); winery trials 1 vintage; natural-wine makers wary of additives
